reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll check the recorded refunds first.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: orders 170, 172, and 175 with the same amounts. Next I'll check the orders list to confirm the refunds are complete and correctly applied before I compute any payouts.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is smaller than its order, so nothing looks wrong. I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme, and won't do the arithmetic myself.
Acme's net balance of 11259 matches my own check against its orders and refund, so the ledger looks consistent. Next I'll get the net balance for birch.
Acme (11259) and birch (18633) both match my own check against the orders and refunds. Cobalt has two refunds, so I'll get its net balance next to confirm it is consistent.

All three net balances match my own check against the orders and refunds: acme 11259, birch 18633, cobalt 54502. The ledger refunds match Alpha's handoff, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 11259 is recorded. Birch (11886 + 6747 = 18633, no refunds) and cobalt (27875 + 37119 - 7535 - 2957 = 54502) both match the net balances, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Birch's payout was recorded. Cobalt's net balance of 54502 matches my check (27875 + 37119 - 7535 - 2957), so I'll record its payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each matches its net balance and my own check against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the report.
